name: Will a garage conversion increase my property taxes?

mainEntity.name: How much can property taxes go up after a garage conversion in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: How much can property taxes go up after a garage conversion in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: Property tax impact is a major concern because a garage conversion can change both the size and function of the home. A simple cosmetic update may have a smaller effect than a fully permitted ADU with plumbing, kitchen, bathroom, and independent living features. The exact tax change depends on how the county values the improvement rather than on the cost of construction alone. Homeowners should expect that a legal, high-value addition may be reassessed at least in part, especially if it materially increases the home’s market value. The tax question should be reviewed alongside financing, resale, and rental income. Some owners are surprised when a conversion creates value but also adds ongoing carrying costs. That is not necessarily a bad tradeoff, but it should be understood before building. The best practice is to ask a local tax professional or assessor-facing adviser how similar projects have been treated in the specific city and county. Planning for the long term is more useful than focusing only on the construction budget.
acceptedAnswer.description: A garage conversion can increase assessed value if the project adds new habitable square footage or a legal dwelling unit. The tax impact depends on the scope of the work, the value of the improvement, and how the county assesses the finished project.
